identificationModule.briefTitle: Study to Compare the Efficacy and Safety of F-627 and GRAN®
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Phase III, Multi-Center, Randomized, Open-Label, Active-Controlled Study to Compare the Efficacy and Safety of F-627 and GRAN® in the Prophylactic Treatment for Chemotherapy-Induced Neutropenia

descriptionModule.briefSummary: A Phase III, Multi-Center, Randomized, Open-Label, Active-Controlled Trial to Compare the Efficacy and Safety of Recombinant Human Granulocyte Colony Stimulating Factor-Fc Fusion Protein (F-627) and Recombinant Human Granulocyte Colony Stimulating Factor (GRAN®) in the Prophylactic Treatment for Chemotherapy-Induced Neutropenia
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
Study Stage: Phase III

Study Population: Female patients with breast cancer will be enrolled to receive at least 4 cycles of Epirubicin + Cyclophosphamide (EC) chemotherapy, that is: epirubicin 100 mg/m\^2 and cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m\^2.

Study Design: A multi-center, randomized, open-label, active-controlled phase III clinical trial

armGroups.label: F-627
armGroups.description: F-627 (20 mg/dose, s.c.) on day 3 of each cycle, i.e., 48 ± 4 h after the start of chemotherapy

armGroups.label: GRAN®
armGroups.description: GRAN® \[5 μg/kg/day, s.c., once daily (± 4 h) up to 2 weeks or until neutrophil count returns to 5.0 × 10\^9/L\] on day 3 of each cycle, i.e., 48 ± 4 h after the start of chemotherapy

interventions.name: F-627
interventions.description: Day 3 of each cycle, i.e., 48 ± 4 h after starting chemotherapy
otherNames: Recombinant Human Granulocyte Colony Stimulating Factor-Fc Fusion Protein

interventions.name: GRAN®
interventions.description: Since day 3 of each cycle, i.e., 48 ± 4 h after starting chemotherapy, continuous treatment for ≤ 2 weeks or until ANC recovers to 5.0 × 10\^9/L from nadir (investigators may refer to ANC test results from the Department of Laboratory Medicine of each study sites to decide when to discontinue GRAN®)

primaryOutcomes.measure: Duration of Grade 3 or 4 Neutropenia (ANC <1.0×10^9/L) in Cycle 1
primaryOutcomes.description:
Grade 3 defined as ANC \<1.0×10\^9/L and Grade 4 defined as ANC\<0.5×10\^9/L. According to the study protocol, the outcome measure "Duration of Grade 3 or 4 Neutropenia (days)" applied to all participants with a valid ANC level, rather than those with an ANC level of \< 1.0 × 109/L. The value of 0 represents the participant experienced 0 days with Grade 3 or 4 Neutropenia (days). Whereas exclusion of a participant from the analysis indicates a lack of ANC data of the participant.

The mean value was calculated as the sum of the durations (days) of ANC \< 1.0 × 109/L for all participants with valid ANC level (the numerator) divided by the number of participants (the denominator).
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Cycle 1, the first of 4, 21-day chemotherapy cycles (average 3 weeks)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: The Absolute Neutrophil Counts (ANC) Nadir From Day 3 to Day 13 of Cycle 1
secondaryOutcomes.description: The minimum value of ANC measured from day 3 to day 13 of cycle 1
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From day 3 to day 13 of cycle 1 (11 days)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Number of Participants With Febrile Neutropenia (FN) in Cycle 1
secondaryOutcomes.description: FN is defined as ANC \< 1.0 × 10\^9/L with fever (a single measurement of body temperature \>38.3 °C or body temperature ≥ 38.0 °C for more than 1 hr).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Cycle 1, the first of 4, 21-day chemotherapy cycles (average 3 weeks)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Time (Days) of ANC Nadir Recovers to 2.0 × 10^9/L in Cycle 1
secondaryOutcomes.description: If the ANC nadir during the first 13 days of the cycle is \< 2.0 × 10\^9/L, the recovery time = ((date of ANC ≥ 2.0 ×10\^9/L) - (date of ANC reaching nadir within the cycle) + 1). If the ANC nadir in the first 13 days of the cycle is ≥2.0 × 10\^9/L, then the recovery time = 0 days.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Cycle 1, the first of 4, 21-day chemotherapy cycles (average 3 weeks)
